# 08 · Practice — Generating Functions

## 1. AtCoder ABC 422 G — Balls and Boxes (`Foundation`)

- [Statement](https://atcoder.jp/contests/abc422/tasks/abc422_g) ·
  [official editorial](https://atcoder.jp/contests/abc422/editorial/13841) · English/Japanese
- Train: decide OGF versus EGF from distinguishability and translate products.

<details><summary>Hint 1</summary>Write a generating function for the choices contributed by one box.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 2</summary>Ask whether assigning labels to two groups introduces a binomial coefficient.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 3</summary>Factorial-scale EGF coefficients so the remaining operations become ordinary convolutions.</details>

## 2. AtCoder ABC 300 Ex — Fibonacci: Revisited (`Advanced`)

- [Statement](https://atcoder.jp/contests/abc300/tasks/abc300_h) ·
  [official editorial](https://atcoder.jp/contests/abc300/editorial/6269) · Japanese (formulas/code are language-independent)
- Train: construct a rational OGF for a recurrence and extract a huge coefficient with Bostan--Mori.

<details><summary>Hint 1</summary>Encode the order-`d` recurrence as a denominator polynomial.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 2</summary>Multiply by `Q(-x)` so the new denominator has only even powers.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 3</summary>Keep numerator coefficients with the parity of the requested index, then halve the index.</details>

## 3. Codeforces 438E — The Child and Binary Tree (`Mastery`)

- [Statement](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/438/E) ·
  [official tutorial](https://codeforces.com/blog/entry/12513) · English/Russian · CF 3100
- Train: derive an algebraic GF from recursive weighted trees; FPS square root and inverse.

<details><summary>Hint 1</summary>Let `W` mark the permitted weight of the root and `F` include the empty tree.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 2</summary>An ordered pair of child trees contributes `F^2`, hence `F=1+W F^2`.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 3</summary>Select the quadratic-formula branch with constant coefficient one.</details>

## 4. Codeforces 960G — Bandit Blues (`Mastery`)

- [Statement](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/960/G) ·
  [official tutorial](https://codeforces.com/blog/entry/58802) · English/Russian · CF 2900
- Train: permutation records, unsigned Stirling numbers, factorial-scaled convolution.

<details><summary>Hint 1</summary>Condition on the position/value of the global maximum.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 2</summary>Left-to-right maxima and cycles of a permutation share the same Stirling distribution.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 3</summary>The final sum over a split point is a convolution after factorial scaling/reversal.</details>

## 5. Codeforces 1342F — Make It Ascending (`Capstone`)

- [Statement](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1342/F) ·
  [official tutorial](https://codeforces.com/blog/entry/76633) · English/Russian · CF 3000
- Train: derive an implicit GF and apply Lagrange inversion together with FFT.

<details><summary>Hint 1</summary>Group histories by the component containing a distinguished element.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 2</summary>Express the recursive component class as a functional equation `T=x Phi(T)`.</details>
<details><summary>Hint 3</summary>Use Lagrange--Bürmann to turn the target coefficient into a coefficient of a power, then batch the resulting sums by convolution.</details>
